title: How much of Earth's water is fresh?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How much of the world's water can we drink?

explain.say: Earth is a watery planet, but almost all its water, about 97.5 percent, is salty seawater that we cannot drink or use to water crops.

draw.text: How much of Earth's water is fresh?

explain.say: Of the small fresh share, most is locked up as ice in Antarctica, Greenland and glaciers, about 1.7 percent of all Earth's water.
Most of the rest is groundwater, hidden in rocks and soil underground, about 0.75 percent.
Lakes, rivers and swamps, the water we see and use most easily, hold only about 0.03 percent of all water. That is why saving and sharing fresh water matters so much.

faq.q: How much of Earth's water is fresh?
faq.a: Only about 2.5 percent. The other 97.5 percent is salty, mostly in the oceans.
asks: Is most water on Earth salty?

faq.a: About two thirds of fresh water is frozen in ice sheets and glaciers, mostly in Antarctica and Greenland. Nearly all the rest is groundwater.
asks: Where is Earth's fresh water stored?

faq.a: Seawater has so much salt that your kidneys would need more water to get rid of it than the seawater gives you, so drinking it makes you more dehydrated.
asks: What happens if you drink salt water?

faq.q: Can we turn seawater into fresh water?
faq.a: Yes, by desalination, which removes salt by boiling or by pushing water through very fine filters. It works but uses a lot of energy, so it is mostly used in dry places that can afford it.

faq.q: Can Earth run out of water?
faq.a: Earth keeps the same water, recycling it through the water cycle. But usable fresh water in a place can run short when people use it faster than rain refills it.

facts: About 97.5 percent of Earth's water is salt water.
Lakes and rivers hold only about 0.03 percent of all Earth's water.
